cases.foot: Odds: the game’s own. Values: collected sale medians, 0 sales across 0 of 0 rolls (0%). Break: how often that tier is worth dismantling rather than listing. Each piece counts at whichever is worth more, under the same bar the Sort tab uses, so this assumes you sort every piece rather than listing all of them. 6 tier(s) have no sale data and are treated as worthless, so this is a floor. Selling what you open moves these prices, and the more you open at once the more it moves them.

sort.gate: A roll needs 0.1 over scrap. That is 0.100 (7.4%) on a Common and 0.10 (0.03%) on a Mythic.
sort.foot: Cut lines move with the scrap price, so they are computed fresh, not written down. 0 of 0 rolls with sale history clear the bar. Right-hand figure is how many of that slot’s seen rolls do. Open a slot and “list at” is the median of that roll’s own recent sales, dimmed where fewer than 5 of them set it.
sort.detail: A roll only earns a listing if it beats what its own scraps fetch. Below the cut line, breaking it is worth more than selling it.
